summary: Construct the character-admissible quotient of perverse sheaves on an abelian variety and its arithmetic and geometric convolution groups. Compute smooth ample hypersurface dimensions and Hodge data, use microlocal factorization and exterior-weight counting to classify connected derived monodromy, and obtain generic and Galois-uniform product monodromy for families. The period-map application records the precise dimension and trace-compatibility obligations that its proof still needs.

nodes.title: Geometric character space
nodes.statement: For an abelian variety A over a characteristic-zero field k, a chosen algebraic closure k̄, and coefficient field F=Q̄_ℓ, put Π(A)=Hom_cont(π₁ᵉᵗ(A_k̄,0),F×). It is an abelian group under multiplication of characters. For a positive-dimensional abelian subvariety B⊂A_k̄, let T_B be the subgroup of characters trivial on the image of π₁ᵉᵗ(B,0). A torsion character has finite image; a torsion coset is τT_B with τ of finite order. On A^c use abelian subvarieties of A^c, including those coupling coordinates. This is a set with group structure; it is not asserted to be an algebraic F-torus.
hypotheses: char(k)=0; ℓ is a prime; all fundamental groups are geometric and based at the identity.
proofSteps: Import the geometric étale fundamental group, its finite-cover equivalence and the torsion/isogeny description for abelian varieties. Define the subgroup as a restriction kernel.
Use π₁(A×A′)=π₁(A)×π₁(A′) to identify product characters. Keep the algebraic Betti-character torus and continuous étale characters distinct.

With the symmetry inherited from complexes, including Koszul signs, this is a rigid symmetric monoidal structure. Its unit is δ₀ and its dual is K∨=[−1]*D_AK. Evaluation and coevaluation satisfy both triangle identities.

proofSteps: Obtain associativity, unit and symmetry by proper base change, the projection formula and the group law. Use the coherent six-operation comparisons, rather than equality of chosen derived models.
Construct evaluation from duality and the antidiagonal, as in Weissauer’s rigidity proposition; verify both triangle identities before passing to a quotient.

nodes.title: Generic vanishing on abelian varieties
nodes.statement: For a perverse F-sheaf K on a complex abelian variety, there is a finite union of translates of proper character subtori outside which H^j(A,K⊗Lχ)=0 for j≠0. The translating characters can be chosen torsion when K is semisimple of geometric origin. The same existence statement for continuous étale characters follows by the comparison and coefficient interfaces. A finite family of perverse sheaves admits one common good character; arbitrary non-geometric sheaves do not acquire torsion exceptional translates by this theorem.
hypotheses: For the torsion-coset assertion impose geometric origin; use the integral-lattice essential image in analytic/étale comparison.
proofSteps: Use KW Theorem 1.1 for the cohomological vanishing and Lemma 11.2(c) for torsion translation in the geometric-origin case.
For finitely many composition factors take the union of their bad loci. Finite unions remain proper and admit continuous good characters; torsion good characters exist in the geometric-origin case.

Then Pχ is Serre and its essential image in P/N is equivalent to Pχ/Nχ. That image contains δ₀ and is closed under quotient convolution and rigid duals. A fixed χ suffices for a tensor category generated by any K belonging to Pχ.

nodes.title: Arithmetic and geometric convolution categories
nodes.statement: Fix χ∈Π(A). Let C_ar be the full subcategory of Pχ/Nχ represented by geometrically semisimple perverse sheaves on A. Let C_geo be the full subcategory on A_k̄ consisting of direct summands of pullbacks of these objects. Both, with ωχ, are neutral Tannakian. For geometrically semisimple representatives K,L the quotient Hom is Hom_P(K,L) modulo maps factoring through N. C_geo is deliberately the category generated by arithmetic pullbacks, rather than the entire geometric perverse quotient.
hypotheses: k has characteristic zero. Geometric semisimplicity is imposed on pullbacks, not on the arithmetic representation at the origin. LS state Lemma 2.7 for every geometrically semisimple object; its closure under convolution then needs Kashiwara’s conjecture (request R3). Restricted to objects of geometric origin, which contain every object used in SC.3–SC.9, the decomposition theorem EDC.7/decomposition-theorem-complex suffices.
proofSteps: Split each geometrically semisimple object into its negligible and nonnegligible geometric parts; Galois-stable isotypic projectors descend. This proves the Hom formula without asserting it for arbitrary objects.

Convolution is proper pushforward along addition. proofSteps: Use the imported abelian Riemann–Roch formula and vanishing to identify the positive integer d; the trivial tangent bundle and normal sequence give e_top(H) with the displayed sign.

For two generators restrict to a common open U⊂V on which both Gauss maps are finite flat, take their fibre product, push its cycle forward along addition A×A×U→A×U with generic degrees and multiplicities, and take the unique clean closure. Extend bilinearly to obtain ◦. This is a commutative ring with unit Λ_{0}; deg(Λ₁◦Λ₂)=degΛ₁ degΛ₂.

nodes.title: Simplicity modulo the centre
nodes.statement: If n>2 and H is a smooth ample divisor on A with trivial translation stabilizer, G_H° is simple modulo its centre; equivalently its nonzero derived Lie algebra is simple. This holds whether or not H is a translate of its inverse image under inversion.
hypotheses: n>2 is needed for the Albanese/Lefschetz step.
proofSteps: Assuming failure of simplicity, factor [m]_*Λ_H as two effective clean cycles of degree >1. Trivial stabilizer makes [m]|H generically injective, hence the left side remains reduced and irreducible.

Use the rational maps from the support factorization, extend them to maps from H to A, and factor them through Alb(H)=A by weak Lefschetz (dim H≥2). The addition identity becomes an identity of homomorphisms plus translation.

Write g₁:A→B₁ for the induced surjective homomorphism and Z₁ for the image of H. If Z₁=B₁ its Gauss degree is zero. Otherwise H is an irreducible component of g₁⁻¹Z₁ by dimension. The connected kernel preserves every such component; a positive-dimensional kernel would preserve the ample divisor, which is impossible. Thus g₁ is an isogeny onto A. Trivial stabilizer makes its restriction H→Z₁ generically one-to-one: outside the intersections with finitely many distinct kernel translates there are no collisions. Isogeny pushforward of conormals therefore preserves the Gauss degree N, forcing the other clean factor to have degree 1. There is no need to infer that g₁ is an isomorphism, a stronger step not justified by the printed full-preimage assertion.

nodes.title: Hodge constraint on exterior powers
nodes.statement: If G_H* is the image of SL_m acting on ∧^k of its standard representation, with 1<k<m−1, then there exist integer weights w:Fin(m)→Z and s∈Z such that W(w,k,s+q)=dA(n,q) for every q∈Z. hypotheses: Smooth ample H of dimension n−1 over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field; trivial translation stabilizer; use compatible complex and p-adic realizations.
proofSteps: Choose a finite-order good character and a finitely generated field of definition. Spread the finite normalizer tensor constraints and specialize to a number-field point, retaining the inclusion of the arithmetic image in the exterior-power normalizer.

Use the requested Hodge–Tate cocharacter in the Zariski closure of the Galois image. Compare its graded fibre functor with the ordinary fibre functor over C_p; this comparison is required and is not a canonical equality of fibres.

The normalizer of the image of SL_m in GL(∧^k) has identity component the image of GL_m (its centralizer is scalar by Schur’s lemma, and every scalar is a k-th power), the kernel of GL_m on ∧^k is μ_k, and its component group has order at most two, nontrivial only when m=2k, since an outer automorphism exchanges ∧^k with ∧^(m−k).

The connected cocharacter lands in the connected exterior-power normalizer. After pulling it back by t↦t^k, lift to GL_m. The lifted standard weights are congruent modulo k because their differences are adjoint weights. Remove their common fractional part into an integral central shift s. Reverse signs to match the native weights −q with the source’s q labels.
Count k-subsets of the resulting integer weights and apply the Hodge–Tate row. For complementary exponent use W-complement and A(n,q)=A(n,n−1−q).

Let v be the greatest occupied weight of u_min and v′ the least of u_max. Then v≤v′, u_min fills all h below v and none above, u_max fills all h above v′ and none below, and Σ_{i<v}(v−i)h(i)+Σ_{i>v′}(i−v′)h(i)+k(v′−v)=n−1. Every summand is nonnegative.

nodes.title: Rigidity of constant tensor constituents
nodes.statement: Let X/C be smooth connected, A/C an abelian variety, and Y⊂X×A a smooth proper family of ample hypersurfaces. On A_η̄ let K=i_*F[n−1], G=G(K), G*=(G°)^der. Assume the geometric generic hypersurface has trivial translation stabilizer, G* is noncommutative connected simple with irreducible distinguished representation, and the family is not generically a translate of a fixed hypersurface by a section of A (equivalently here after spreading the unique translation). If a simple object in ⟨K⟩⊗ has a representative pulled back from A_C, then G* acts trivially on it.

proofSteps: Compare two independent geometric generic fibres over X². Goursat gives either independent simple derived factors or a graph relation modulo scalars.

In the independent case a constant constituent is pulled back in both ways, so both simple factors act trivially. In the graph case use enough independent points of X^r to kill the finite outer-automorphism ambiguity.

The remaining scalar relation gives a one-dimensional factor between the two distinguished objects. Identify it with a skyscraper, hence translation. Trivial stabilizer makes the translating section unique and allows descent, contradicting the nonconstant hypothesis.

nodes.title: Jordan’s theorem on finite linear groups
nodes.statement: For every n≥1 there is an integer J(n) with the following property. If F is a field of characteristic zero and Γ⊂GL_n(F) is a finite subgroup, then Γ has an abelian normal subgroup of index at most J(n). Consequently, if F is algebraically closed of characteristic zero, V is an n-dimensional F-vector space and B⊂GL(V) is a subgroup whose image in PGL(V) is finite, then B has an abelian normal subgroup of index at most J(n), and every irreducible finite-dimensional representation of B over F has dimension at most J(n).
hypotheses: Characteristic zero is essential: in characteristic p the groups SL_2(F_q)⊂GL_2(F̄_p) have no abelian subgroups of index bounded independently of q.
proofSteps: The entries of a finite Γ generate a finitely generated field, which embeds in ℂ, so assume F=ℂ. Averaging a Hermitian form over Γ conjugates Γ into U(n).

Commutators shrink near the identity: for g,h∈U(n), ‖[g,h]−1‖≤2‖g−1‖‖h−1‖. Hence the elements of Γ within a fixed small distance of 1 generate an abelian normal subgroup, and a volume-packing count of its cosets in U(n) bounds the index in terms of n alone (the Bieberbach–Frobenius argument).

For B finite modulo scalars, Γ₁=(F^×B)∩SL(V) is finite (its image in PGL(V) is finite and its kernel is μ_n) and F^×B=F^×Γ₁. If A₁⊲Γ₁ is abelian of index at most J(n), then B∩F^×A₁ is abelian, normal in B and of index at most J(n). On an irreducible representation W, a common eigenvector of this abelian normal subgroup and its translates by coset representatives span a B-stable subspace of dimension at most J(n), so dim W≤J(n).
acceptance: For n=1 every finite subgroup is abelian, so J(1)=1 works.
The quaternion group Q₈⊂GL₂(ℂ) is not abelian; its cyclic subgroup of order 4 is abelian, normal and of index 2.
The dihedral groups of order 2q in GL₂(ℂ) have their rotation subgroup of index 2 for every q: the bound depends on n only.
The statement fails in characteristic p for SL₂(F_q)⊂GL₂(F̄_p), so the characteristic-zero hypothesis cannot be dropped.

uses.how: bounds the dimension of irreducible representations of a subgroup of N(G*) that is finite modulo scalars, ruling out irreducible action on a large test representation W

nodes.title: Finite representations detecting a simple product
nodes.statement: Let G* be a noncommutative connected simple algebraic group over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field acting faithfully and irreducibly on V, and let N=N_GL(V)(G*). For c≥1 construct a finite list T of irreducible representations of N^c with no (G*)^c-invariants such that for every reductive algebraic subgroup B⊂N^c, (G*)^c⊂B iff T^B=0 for every T in the list. Choose a Jordan bound J for subgroups of N finite modulo scalars and an N-representation W of dimension >J restricting irreducibly to G*. Take the irreducible constituents of End(W)/F and End(Lie G*)/F in each coordinate, and the cross-coordinate representations Lie(G*)_i⊗Lie(G*)_j∨ for i<j.
hypotheses: Reductivity of B and characteristic zero are essential; the normalizer and all tensor constructions use the actual faithful image.
proofSteps: Take J from Jordan’s theorem, SC.7/jordan-finite-linear-groups. For W take the Cartan component of highest weight rλ in Sym^r V for large r, where λ is the highest weight of V: it is irreducible under G*, stable under N because N fixes the isomorphism class of V and hence λ, and its dimension grows without bound by the Weyl dimension formula (Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight Layer 6, cited as it stands). No invariants in the two endomorphism tests makes each coordinate projection act irreducibly on W and on the adjoint module.

nodes.title: Big monodromy for generic simultaneous twists
nodes.statement: In the family setting of constant-part-rigidity, assume the geometric generic stabilizer is trivial and G* is connected simple with irreducible distinguished representation. For every c≥1 there is a finite union S of torsion cosets in Π(A)^c such that for (χ₁,…,χ_c) outside S, R^j f_*(g*Lχ_i)=0 for j≠n−1 and the geometric monodromy of ⊕_i R^(n−1)f_*(g*Lχ_i) contains (G*)^c as a normal subgroup. On this product it is the direct sum of the c distinguished representations, each supported on its own factor. Here f:Y→X,g:Y→A are the projections. All sheaves are lisse on X by smooth proper base change.
hypotheses: X is smooth connected over C; f is smooth proper with smooth ample hypersurface fibres; the family is not generically constant up to translation.
proofSteps: First remove concentration failures for the c twists. Arithmetic normalization places the simultaneous monodromy group inside N(G*)^c.

Realize the finite detecting tensor representations by geometrically semisimple perverse objects in the arithmetic axis-generated category. Their geometric constituents have no constant part by independent-coordinate-factors.

Apply relative-generic-vanishing to all those objects. For torsion characters the sheaves g*Lχ have geometric origin, so the decomposition theorem EDC.7/decomposition-theorem-complex makes the local systems semisimple and the monodromy group reductive. The finite test battery forces product containment; the normalizer inclusion makes the contained product normal.

nodes.title: Prime-to-p Frobenius avoidance
nodes.statement: Let A/K be an abelian variety over a number field with good reduction at a place of residue characteristic p, fix lifts of its Frobenius in the two actions on finite-order character pairs, and choose m>0 whose Frobenius power fixes the Galois closure of K. Given c≥1 and a finite union S of torsion cosets in Π(A)^c, there is a finite union S′ of torsion cosets in Π(A) such that for each finite-order χ of order prime to p outside S′, some e₁,…,e_c∈Z give (Frob_p^(me₁)χ,…,Frob_p^(me_c)χ) outside S. The two actions are geometric transport and cyclotomic transport of character values.
hypotheses: Only prime-to-p torsion characters are asserted here. Fix a common algebraic closure and compatible embeddings for the transport.
proofSteps: Let M be the number of cosets in S. The case M=0 is immediate. Replace m by a multiple so the geometric restriction kernels and translating torsion data are stable under σ=Frob^m. On every prime-to-p Tate module the combined geometric/cyclotomic action has Weil eigenvalues of nonzero weight, so no positive power has eigenvalue 1.

For a fixed proper coset τT in Π(A)^c, choose a coordinate axis whose inverse image T_r is proper. Write T_r as the restriction kernel for a positive-dimensional B⊂A. For every 0≤e<e′≤M, equality of σ^eχ and σ^e′χ on B forces χ|B into a finite torsion set: the relevant σ^(e′−e)−1 has nonzero determinant. Taking inverse images under restriction gives a finite union of torsion translates of T_r. Collect these collision loci for all cosets and exponent pairs into S′.

For χ outside S′, fix all exponents other than e_r in {0,…,M}. At most one e_r can place the tuple in τT; two choices would give an excluded collision on B. Thus at most (M+1)^(c−1) tuples are bad for each coset and at most M(M+1)^(c−1)<(M+1)^c are bad in total. A good tuple exists. Exponents for the original Frobenius step are obtained by the integer scaling used when enlarging m.
The determinant argument here concerns prime-to-p torsion only. E6 records the omitted p-primary justification in the source, and E20 corrects the reversed word in its initial finite-box count.

sources.match: This is the form justified by the prime-to-p Tate-module argument and sufficient for Corollary 4.10 after choosing ℓ≠p.

acceptance: The Frobenius powers e_i may depend on χ and may be negative.
Do not apply the proof to arbitrary p-power characters.

nodes.title: Character generic in every conjugate
nodes.statement: For each embedding ι:K→Q̄ suppose S_ι is a finite union of torsion cosets in Π(A_ι). For any chosen prime ℓ there are an embedding ι and a finite-order ℓ-power character χ on A_ι such that every conjugate (ι′,χ′) under Gal(Q̄/Q)×Gal(Q^cyc/Q) avoids S_ι′. This lemma alone has no ℓ≠p condition; that condition is imposed when combining it with Frobenius avoidance.
hypotheses: Character values are finite-order roots of unity; the cyclotomic action on values is defined on this torsion character set.
proofSteps: Take the finite Galois/cyclotomic conjugate closure of the torsion-coset data, using finite fields of definition of abelian subvarieties and translating torsion characters.

Among characters of order dividing ℓ^r, the total count is ℓ^(2nr). A restriction kernel from a positive-dimensional abelian subvariety has at most a fixed multiple of ℓ^(2(n−1)r) points. For large r the finite exceptional union cannot exhaust all characters.
The source counts ℓ^(2kn) characters of order dividing ℓ^k but calls them ℓ^(2k)-torsion; the count used is for ℓ^k-torsion (finding E23).

sources.match: The counting is uniform over every conjugate pair; the exceptional data is finite and the codimension estimate is decisive.

acceptance: For a simple elliptic curve, each proper torsion coset is a point, while the number of ℓ^r characters grows as ℓ^(2r).
Choosing a character generic only for one embedding is insufficient.

nodes.title: Uniform big monodromy on a character orbit
nodes.statement: Let the family Y⊂X×A and the hypotheses of generic-big-monodromy be defined over a number field K. Fix c≥1, a good-reduction place of residue characteristic p, m>0 as in Frobenius avoidance and a prime ℓ≠p. Then some embedding ι and an ℓ-power finite-order character χ have the following property for every Gal(Q̄/Q)×Gal(Q^cyc/Q)-conjugate (ι′,χ′): R^j f_*(g*Lχ′)=0 for j≠n−1, and there exist e₁,…,e_c∈Z for which the geometric monodromy of the sum twisted by Frob_p^(me_i)χ′ contains (G*)^c normally, with the c distinguished actions. The exponents may depend on the conjugate.
hypotheses: The Frobenius and cyclotomic lifts are fixed once; ℓ is the order prime of the finite character, and need not equal the cohomological prime.
proofSteps: Apply the generic simultaneous-twist theorem to the finitely many embedding-conjugate families.
Use Frobenius avoidance to turn each c-fold bad set into a one-character bad set, adding the single-character concentration loci.
Choose an ℓ-power character whose every conjugate avoids all of these one-character sets. Its order is prime to p, so every conjugate satisfies the corrected avoidance theorem.

sources.match: The uniform conclusion survives the correction of Lemma 4.8 by choosing ℓ≠p. This is the arithmetic output consumed by the Lawrence–Venkatesh Part II direction.

acceptance: The conclusion is a product (G*)^c with specified action, rather than a single G*.
The theorem does not choose one exponent tuple valid for every conjugate.

nodes.title: Period maps of isogeny pullbacks
nodes.statement: Fix a complex abelian variety A of dimension n≥2 and an ample line bundle L. Let M be the open subset of the complete linear system P(H⁰(A,L)) parameterizing smooth divisors, using the convention that points are nonzero sections modulo scalar. For m>0 let Y_m→M be the family [m]⁻¹H. The torsion-free integral middle cohomology with its polarization and Hodge filtration defines a period map Φ_m to the appropriate polarized period quotient. Its rational local system splits, after a coefficient extension, into character-isotypic summands H^(n−1)(H,Lχ), for characters of A[m]. The fixed class is in Pic(A), not merely NS(A).
hypotheses: Use polarizations from the fixed ample geometric data and finite level/markings when a period domain rather than its quotient is used.
proofSteps: Form the smooth-divisor open of the projective section space. Multiplication by m is finite étale in characteristic zero, so the pulled-back universal divisor is smooth proper.

Import the polarized integral variation and its period map, keeping the lattice modulo torsion. Decompose the finite abelian deck group after scalar extension; trace and pullback maps compare the variations for m|m′.

nodes.title: Surface period finiteness by Torelli
nodes.statement: When dim A=2, the period map Φ₁ of smooth curves in the fixed complete linear system |L| has finite fibres. Here the polarization on H¹ is the canonical cup-product principal polarization. The genus is g=1+d≥2. No convolution simplicity assertion in dimension two is required.
hypotheses: A is a complex abelian surface, L is ample, and the parameter space is the smooth-divisor open M⊂|L|; the statement is vacuous when M is empty.
proofSteps: Use adjunction and the SC.3 Euler calculation to obtain g=1+d. A polarized integral weight-one Hodge structure determines the principally polarized Jacobian. The full-level Torelli theorem gives finite geometric fibres from the moduli of genus-g curves to the moduli of their polarized Jacobians.

Show that M→M_g has zero-dimensional geometric fibres. On a reduced connected component of such a fibre, the universal curve becomes a fixed curve C after the finite étale isomorphism cover; finite automorphisms for g≥2 and a fine level N≥3 justify this reduction. Fix c₀∈C. The pointed map C→A uniquely factors through J(C) by Abel–Jacobi, and the relative Hom space is unramified, so its homomorphism component is constant on a connected reduced parameter space.

Consequently the embedded images in A on that component differ only by translations. Translating a fixed divisor H₀ preserves O_A(H₀)≅L only for points in ker φ_L. Amplitude makes this kernel finite; hence the component has constant image in M. The fibre of M→M_g is a zero-dimensional finite-type algebraic space, so has finitely many geometric points.

Combine these finite fibres with Torelli and the weight-one comparison. Passing to and forgetting a finite level cover preserves fibre finiteness. This gives m=1 for n=2 and repairs the dimension mismatch in the source period proof.

sources.match: The pointed Abel–Jacobi map has the Albanese universal property for maps to abelian varieties; Torelli recovers a curve, up to the stated sign and translation, from its canonically polarized Jacobian.
States quasi-finiteness for n≥2; its proof invokes Lemma 3.9, which needs n>2, so the surface case is supplied separately here (finding E18).

A positive-dimensional translation orbit cannot lie in this fixed |L|.
The Hodge-bundle-only comparison is insufficient; R16 requires the polarized integral H¹ comparison.

nodes.title: Quasi-finite isogeny-pullback period map
nodes.statement: For the smooth-divisor space M of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety of dimension n≥2, some m>0 makes Φ_m quasi-finite, meaning every fibre is finite. For n=2 take m=1 by surface-period-finiteness. For n>2 the monodromy route passes to the finite generic translation-stabilizer quotient and retains the marked-period compatibility obligation G3. The general assertion is a target with that recorded proof obligation.
hypotheses: This is a target theorem with recorded proof gaps, not an implementation or a completed proof.
proofSteps: On M×M use the weight-zero Hom variation and the flat orbit of the diagonal identity tensor. CDK Corollary 1.3 makes its projected Hodge locus Z_m closed algebraic: multiply a rational tensor by a fixed denominator and use its fixed polarization norm to apply the finite bounded-norm theorem. A countable-union Hodge-locus statement alone would not suffice.

For m|m′ the trace-compatible identity condition gives Z_m′⊂Z_m. Along divisibility, Noetherianity gives a stabilized closed relation. A positive-dimensional period fibre then supplies an algebraic positive-dimensional family with constant period for every multiple of m. Integral polarizability makes its monodromy finite, and the deck-character decomposition makes every torsion-twist summand have finite monodromy.

Fixing L rules out constancy by translations. Quotient by the finite generic translation stabilizer, shrinking the family so that its action is fixed; the resulting ample family has trivial stabilizer. For n>2 apply simplicity and generic-big-monodromy to contradict finite monodromy for a torsion character outside the finite exceptional union.

For n=2 apply surface-period-finiteness instead. For n>2, G3 must certify that the chosen identity-orbit relations preserve every pullback/trace summand, are nested under divisibility and detect period fibres with the specified polarized marking conventions. Identity transport respects flat trace idempotents, but this must be reconciled with the quotient used for the period map.

sources.match: Uses closed projected identity Hodge loci, their stabilization along divisibility and the big monodromy theorem to contradict a positive-dimensional fibre.

The locus of integral (0,0) classes of bounded polarization norm is algebraic and finite over the base; the points where some determination of a flat integral section is of type (0,0) form an algebraic subvariety.

acceptance: Quasi-finite is fibre finiteness, not global injectivity or properness.
Only Picard-fixed parameter spaces are in scope.
The n=2 proof uses Torelli and rigid Hom spaces, with no appeal to the n>2 simplicity lemma.
